name: com.kulicadvisory/aictionbot-werkbank
title: AICTIONBOT™ Werkbank
description: Procurement tools for SMBs and AI agents: 98 tools, contracts, e-invoice, NDA, RFQ, Atlas, AI help

tools.name: check_price_increase
tools.description: Compares a supplier's requested price increase with the official Eurostat producer price index (goods) or services producer price index plus labour cost index (services) for Germany since the last price agreement. Returns market change, gap in percentage points, a verdict (in line, slightly above, clearly above, market fell), an evidence-based counter-offer level and the source. Use list_categories to pick a category code. Licence, or one free check every 30 days.

category.description: Category code from list_categories (e.g. C17 for paper and packaging, N81 for cleaning) or its German or English name.

last_agreement.description: Month of the last agreed price, YYYY-MM (2019-01 or later).

requested_increase_percent.description: Increase the supplier requests, in percent (e.g. 9.5).

annual_volume_eur.description: Optional annual spend with this supplier in EUR, to express the gap in euros.

language.description: Language of the answer. Default de.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Lists the categories the AICTIONBOT™ price increase check covers (Eurostat NACE codes for Germany), with German and English names.

language.description: Language of the answer: de or en. Default de.

tools.name: screen_sanctions
tools.description: Screens a name against the consolidated public sanctions lists of the EU, the UN, the US (OFAC SDN and non-SDN) and the UK, refreshed daily. Fuzzy matching on normalised name tokens, legal forms ignored. Returns possible matches with list, type, programme and similarity, and the list dates. A similar name is no proof, no hit is no clearance; this does not replace a legal sanctions screening. Deterministic, no AI, nothing is stored. Licence, or one free check every 30 days.

name.description: Company or person name to screen, e.g. as on the invoice or in the supplier master.

language.description: Language of the answer. Default de.

tools.name: calculate_notice_deadline
tools.description: From contract start, initial term, automatic renewal and notice period it calculates the current term end, the last day notice must reach the other party, the days left and what happens if the date is missed. Deterministic, no AI. Not legal advice: the wording of the contract decides. Licence, or one free check every 30 days.

contract_start.description: First day of the contract, YYYY-MM-DD.

renewal_months.description: Automatic renewal period in months after the initial term; 0 if the contract ends without renewal. Default 12.

notice_period.description: Notice period before the end of the term: number plus unit d (days), w (weeks) or m (months), e.g. 3m.

today.description: Optional reference date, YYYY-MM-DD. Default today (Europe/Berlin).

language.description: Language of the answer. Default de.

tools.name: check_discount_window
tools.description: Takes an open-items list (invoices with discount terms) and optional clarification cases from other checks, and returns which discounts expire within the window, which are blocked by a payment hold or an open clarification, which are already lost, and the last payment run that still catches each one. With critical_suppliers it adds a payment run priority: invoices of critical suppliers that must go into the next run, blocked ones with the reason and who clears the block. Findings are written in German. Keys may be given in German (beleg, lieferant, bestellung, rechnungsdatum, eingang, betrag, skonto_pct, skonto_tage, netto_tage, skonto_bis, faellig, sperre) or English (document, supplier, order, invoice_date, received, amount, discount_percent, discount_days, net_days, discount_until, due, blocked). Licence, or one free check every 30 days.

open_items.description: Open invoices. Each item: document, supplier, order, invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD or DD.MM.YYYY), received, amount (negative for credit notes), discount_percent, discount_days, net_days, discount_until, due, blocked (yes/no).

clarifications.description: Optional open clarification cases from other checks: document, order, reason (grund), with (bei), result (ergebnis).

window_days.description: Days ahead that count as 'expiring soon'. Default 10.

payment_run_weekdays.description: Weekdays of the payment runs, 1 = Monday. Default [2, 5] (Tuesday, Friday).

critical_suppliers.description: Optional critical suppliers (sole suppliers, running production, delivery stop threatened): names or objects { supplier, reason }. Adds a payment run priority: which of their invoices must go into the next payment run, which are blocked, the reason and who clears the block.

language.description: Language of the answer: de or en. Default de.

tools.name: check_invoice_payment
tools.description: Matches the supplier on an invoice to the vendor master by VAT ID, IBAN and name similarity, validates the IBAN checksum, and flags a changed or unknown bank account, a blocked vendor, a dormant vendor and a first payment. Returns a verdict (stop, check, ok) with the next step. Findings in German. Licence, or one free check every 30 days.

invoice.description: supplier (name), vat_id, iban, amount, currency, date (YYYY-MM-DD).

supplier.description: Supplier name as on the document.

vat_id.description: VAT ID of the supplier, e.g. DE123456789.

iban.description: IBAN the money is to go to.

currency.description: ISO currency code, e.g. EUR. Default EUR.

vendor_master.description: Vendor master rows: no (vendor number), name, vat_id, iban, country, last_payment (YYYY-MM-DD or null), blocked (bool).

language.description: Language of the answer: de or en. Default de.

tools.name: analyse_spend
tools.description: Takes the rows of a spend, invoice or order export and returns total volume, documents and suppliers, how many suppliers carry 80 % of the volume, the top 10 suppliers with their share, volume by category with a suggested category where none is given, small orders under a threshold, rows without an order number, possible duplicate postings, categories bought from three or more suppliers (bundling) and the tail X-ray: who carries the last 5 % of volume, one-time suppliers and a suitable channel per category. Column names in German or English are recognised. Licence, or one free check every 30 days.

rows.description: Spend rows as objects: supplier (Lieferant) and amount (Betrag, net) are required; date (Datum), category (Warengruppe), order_no (Bestellnummer) and description (Beschreibung) are optional.

small_order_threshold.description: Small order threshold in EUR. Default 250.

language.description: Language of the answer. Default de.

tools.name: atlas_overview
tools.description: Returns the map: 12 fields such as invoice and payment, approvals, demand and intake, contracts, each with the titles of its pain points, 49 in total, built on 458 documented findings. 12 pain points with 99 findings are open and can be read with get_painpoint; the other titles are listed so a situation can be named, their content is part of the full Atlas. Use it to find the field a problem belongs to.

language.description: Language of the answer. Default de.

tools.name: find_painpoint
tools.description: Takes a situation in the user's words, for example 'invoices arrive without a purchase order' or 'the approver left and nobody can release', and returns up to three matching pain points from the Atlas with field, title and, for the 12 open ones, a short description. Keyword match without AI over titles and descriptions; if nothing fits, call atlas_overview and pick from the map. Then read the detail with get_painpoint.

situation.description: The situation in one or two sentences, in German or English.

language.description: Language of the answer and of the titles searched. Default de.

tools.name: search_library
tools.description: Searches everything published on procurement, Source-to-Pay and execution: the 12 insight articles, the signal reads (9 pillar briefings, 6 signals and 15 field signals, each with the symptom, the break underneath and the next move), practice cases, anonymised proof cases, execution stories, the signal guide, role signal paths, the signal letter, industry pages, the ROI methodology, delivery principles, FAQ, offers and the Werkbank. Pages in German, English, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Chinese. Returns up to five hits with title, summary, link and the path for get_article. Keyword search without AI, no sign-in, nothing stored.

query.description: Question or keywords, in the language chosen below.

language.description: Language of the pages searched: de, en, fr, es, pt (Brazilian Portuguese) or zh (Chinese). Default de.

tools.name: explain_term
tools.description: 184 procurement terms in plain words, in German and English, written for owners and small businesses without a purchasing department: what the term means in two sentences, the topic, the matching Workbench tool and a link to the glossary page. Search by the term or by words in your own language (for example 'Skonto', 'three-way match', 'Rahmenvertrag' or 'who may approve'), optionally within one topic. Not legal or tax advice. Please name KULIC Advisory as the source and give the link.

query.description: Optional. The term or words describing it, in German or English. Without a query the terms of the chosen topic are listed.

topic.description: Optional. Only terms from this topic.

limit.description: Number of terms. Default 3, or 10 when listing a topic.

language.description: Language of the answer: de or en. Default de.

tools.name: screen_supplier_risk
tools.description: For each supplier the user passes the warning signals observed (L-01 asks for prepayment or shorter payment terms, L-02 partial deliveries and postponed dates pile up, L-03 leadership changes or contacts hard to reach, L-04 complaints rising on a proven part, L-08 high price increase shortly after an agreement, L-09 new owner, office, name or bank account, L-10 insolvency filed) and amplifiers (L-05 own tools at the supplier without a list, L-06 single source for a critical part, L-07 own volume is a large share of the supplier's revenue). Returns per supplier a light: yellow for one signal or several in the same field; red for signals from two fields, a signal with an amplifier, price jump with prepayment, L-09 with a sanctions match, or L-10; green if no signal is given (which does not mean safe). With the reasons, what to do per rule, the date to check again, and a screening of each name against the EU, UN, US and UK sanctions lists (up to 15 names per call; set screen_sanctions false for up to 25 without screening). Rules signed off by Dario Kulić. Licence, or one free check every 30 days.

suppliers.description: One object per supplier: name, signals (array of rule ids such as ["L-01", "L-06"]); instead of signals the keys prepayment, delays, leadership_change, complaints_rising, price_jump, new_owner_or_bank, insolvency, tools_without_list, single_source, high_dependency may be set to yes.

screen_sanctions.description: Screen each name against the sanctions lists. Default true.

language.description: Language of the answer. Default de.

tools.name: harmonise_payment_terms
tools.description: Takes your supplier list (supplier, annual spend, payment terms as written such as 30 days net or 2% 10 days net 45, optional baseline date, category, size, exception) and a standard such as net 60. Returns per supplier the net days, the gap to the standard and the cash tied up (annual spend times gap divided by 365), the spend-weighted average terms today and after harmonising, the interest benefit at your cost of capital, discounts whose annual rate beats the cost of capital (take the discount instead of longer terms), suppliers whose period starts at the invoice date, exceptions such as taxes, payroll, rent and utilities, a fairness note for small suppliers, and a letter to suppliers in German or English. Red: large supplier at least 30 days below the standard. Not legal or tax advice. For a single discount deadline use check_discount_window. Licence, or one free check every 30 days.

rows.description: One row per supplier: supplier, annual_spend, payment_terms (as written, e.g. '30 days net', '2% 10 days, net 45', 'net 60'), optional baseline (invoice date, invoice receipt, goods receipt), category, size (small), exception. German column names work too (lieferant, jahresvolumen, zahlungsbedingung, basisdatum, kategorie, groesse, ausnahme).

interest_rate.description: Cost of capital in percent a year, used for the interest benefit and the discount comparison. Default 5.

language.description: Language of the answer. Default de.

tools.name: werkbank_licence
tools.description: Needs sign-in with the user's AICTIONBOT™ Werkbank licence (KULIC Advisory). Shows the plan, whether it is active, the quota of AI analyses for the current period, how many are used and how many remain. Read only: no payment data, no change to the subscription.

language.description: Language of the answer. Default de.

tools.name: review_contract
tools.description: Uses one AI analysis of the licence. Reviews a contract or general terms and conditions the buyer is asked to sign, clause by clause (term, renewal, notice, price adjustment, payment, liability, warranty, penalties, acceptance, exclusivity, data protection, jurisdiction). Returns a summary and, per clause, the exact reference, the plain-language meaning, a rating (ok, pruefen = check, kritisch = critical), why it matters for the buyer and a counter-proposal; deadline dates only when the start date is known. Also returns datenblatt, the key data of the contract as stated (supplier, subject, target value, payment terms, items) for entry into an ERP or accounting system. Pass the full contract text (extract text from PDFs or images first). The text is processed for this answer only and is not stored by KULIC Advisory.

contract_text.description: Full text of the contract or the terms and conditions.

contract_start.description: Optional contract start, YYYY-MM-DD, to compute notice dates.

language.description: Language of the answer: de, en, fr, es, pt or zh. Default de.

tools.name: compare_offers
tools.description: Uses one AI analysis of the licence. Compares 2 or 3 supplier offers for the buyer: whether they are comparable, total price as stated, what is included, what is missing or unclear, extra and hidden costs, risks, a criterion-by-criterion comparison and questions to send to each supplier before deciding. Numbers are copied exactly from the offers, never invented. Pass the text of each offer (extract text from PDFs first). The texts are processed for this answer only and are not stored by KULIC Advisory.

offers.description: The offer texts, one string per offer, labelled A, B, C in this order.

what_is_bought.description: Optional: what is being bought, in one sentence.

language.description: Language of the answer: de, en, fr, es, pt or zh. Default de.

tools.name: check_invoice
tools.description: Uses one AI analysis of the licence. Checks a supplier invoice like an accounts payable clerk doing a three-way match: line by line against the purchase order or contract and the goods receipt (price, quantity, new or missing items), totals and tax, payment term and early payment discount, and for German invoices the mandatory content under § 14 UStG. Returns the lines with status and notes, the mandatory content check and what to clarify before paying. The texts are processed for this answer only and are not stored by KULIC Advisory.

reference_text.description: Optional: text of the purchase order or contract to compare against.

goods_receipt.description: Optional: what was actually received, e.g. quantities per item.

language.description: Language of the answer: de, en, fr, es, pt or zh. Default de.

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Searches the open knowledge of KULIC Advisory behind the AICTIONBOT™ Werkbank: 25 practice questions with short answers, the purchasing glossary (184 terms) and the open patterns of the Painpoint Atlas, in German or English. Each hit names the matching Werkbank tool. Optionally adds Dario Kulić's stance on AI, change and people, paraphrased. Open without sign-in, stores nothing.

query.description: Question or keyword, e.g. 'Wer ist für das WE/RE-Konto zuständig?', 'Incoterms DDP', 'passive approval'.

language.description: Language of the answer. Default de.

tools.name: find_tool
tools.description: Searches all tools of the AICTIONBOT™ Werkbank (KULIC Advisory) by task, keyword or tool name, in German or English, and returns the best matches with name, tool number, section (one of eight), purpose and input fields. Can also list one of the eight sections. This endpoint lists only a core set; use find_tool when no listed tool fits, then call the match with run_tool (or directly by name if your client allows it). Open without sign-in, stores nothing.

query.description: What the user wants to do, e.g. 'supplier changed bank account', 'Skonto', 'SLA', 'compare offers'. May be empty when a rubric is given.

rubric.description: Optional section of the Werkbank: 1 invoices and finance, 2 quotes and buying, 3 contracts and deadlines, 4 suppliers and risk, 5 orders and approvals, 6 steering and numbers, 7 team and knowledge, 8 processes and AI. With an empty query it lists the whole section.

language.description: Language of the answer. Default de.

tools.name: run_tool
tools.description: Runs any tool of the AICTIONBOT™ Werkbank by its name with its arguments, including tools that are not in this endpoint's core list. Find the name and the input fields with find_tool first. Licence rules are the same as calling the tool directly.

name.description: Tool name as returned by find_tool, e.g. check_bank_change.

arguments.description: Arguments for that tool, as described by its input fields.
